title: DR1 lets you filter the dashboard to one notification status; the frontend has no status filter.

finding.frontend: The frontend filter panel has one keyword box and a Search button (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/template.njk:38-56). Status appears on every row as a tag but there is no way to filter on it, so finding the drafts among a page of submitted notifications means reading each card.
finding.prototype: DR1 gives status its own collapsible section in the filter panel, holding a select labelled "Status" with eight options: "Select one" and then Draft, Submitted, In progress, Approved, Action required, Rejected and Complete (app/views/dashboard.html:133-161).
finding.difference: Add a status select to the filter form and pass the chosen value through the list read. Two things have to land first: the list endpoint must accept a status filter, and the frontend must have statuses worth filtering by — today it knows only Draft, Submitted, Amending and Deleted, so five of DR1's seven options would return nothing.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a status control in the frontend dashboard's filter panel.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs (dr1-dashboard.html:359-402 renders a select named status with exactly the eight options named; fe-dashboard-populated.html:123-135 renders one input named referenceNumber and a Search button and nothing else) and the fe-dashboard-populated and dr1-dashboard-filters-open screenshots; opened dashboard/template.njk:38-56 and app/views/dashboard.html:134-162. Ran the falsifier by grepping both frontend dashboard captures for a control named or labelled status — the only match is the read-only Status tag in each card, not a filter, so it does not fire. Band needs-backend checked and upheld, and it is stronger than the finding says — see correction. CORRECT.
finding.correction: The claim stands; the slot is left alone and one piece of supporting evidence is added because the finding understates its own blocker. It says the frontend "must have statuses worth filtering by" as though that were a frontend decision. It is not: the real records adapter maps the backend's status through services/persistence/records/real/status.js:15-20, which throws "Unknown backend fulfilment status" for anything outside DRAFT, SUBMITTED, AMEND and DELETED. So five of DR1's seven options cannot merely return nothing — the contract change has to land before the frontend can receive such a status at all. needs-backend is enforced, not just advisable. Minor citation drift, not corrected: the finding cites app/views/dashboard.html:133-161 and the Status details block actually runs 134-162; it resolves to the right content.

relatedTo.why: that one comes first: five of DR1's seven filter options name statuses the frontend cannot yet hold, so the filter is only useful once the statuses exist
